summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his discussion on the book of purification, specifically covering what invalidates tayammum (dry ablution). He explains that the same things that invalidate wudu also invalidate tayammum, with one additional condition: if water becomes available to a person, tayammum immediately becomes invalid. Sh. Ali Mashhour uses a hadith from Abu Said Al-Khudri about two travelers who performed tayammum, then found water. One man repeated his prayer while the other did not. The Prophet (PBUH) approved both actions but noted the second man received double reward for his caution, while the first man's action would now be impermissible since he now knows water was available. Sh. Ali Mashhour then extends this discussion into a profound lesson about the character of the Companions, particularly their humility and avoidance of self-praise. He illustrates how Abu Said narrated the hadith in the third person to avoid any appearance of praising himself, connecting this to broader Islamic teachings about avoiding hidden riya (showing off) and seeking Allah's pleasure over human admiration.
